A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Render-FM CT-to-6DGS rendering work. All pages, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison; relocated and reformatted material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering-quality and efficiency experiments on TotalSegmentator and CT-ORG in Section 4, Table 1, and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds CTPelvic1K results in Appendix A1 and a reported training failure without anatomy-guided priming in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: Both versions use the six-channel nnU-Net-inspired backbone, 37-channel Gaussian prediction, anatomy-guided priming, differentiable 6DGS rendering, L1 plus MS-SSIM loss, and optional fine-tuning. v2 expands implementation explanations without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix A1 adds pelvic CT evaluation on CTPelvic1K, described as representing different institutions, acquisition protocols, and patient populations. TotalSegmentator, CT-ORG, and their existing transfer-function and composability scenarios remain. This extends CT coverage without introducing another imaging modality or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparison set: 6DGS, 6DGS with AGP, Render-FM, and fine-tuned Render-FM. The new CTPelvic1K table evaluates this same set; no additional external comparison method is evaluated.

E3.justification: v1 specifies 40 training views for composability, comprising 20 full-anatomy and 20 skeleton views. v2 describes 20 views per scan without that exception. This changes the reported protocol, although unchanged Table 1 values do not establish rerunning. The added CTPelvic1K evaluation uses the first six scans, a shared renderer, and 300-iteration fine-tuning.

E4.justification: v2 Section 4.2 newly reports that Render-FM fails to converge without AGP, addressing whether priming is necessary for feedforward training. No convergence curves or detailed control settings accompany this finding. The AGP-versus-6DGS numerical comparison was already present in v1, so its relocation into an ablation subsection is not new evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averaging the new CTPelvic1K results over six scans does not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All 16 rows and six numerical metrics in Table 1 are unchanged. v2 Table A1 adds CTPelvic1K results: Render-FM achieves 27.15 dB PSNR in 0.65 seconds, versus 27.95 dB and 1643.32 seconds for 6DGS; fine-tuning yields 33.30 dB in 78.02 seconds. Figure 1 adds illustrative PSNR annotations, and Section 4.2 adds the nonconvergence finding.

T1.justification: The conditional Gaussian mean and covariance, directional opacity modulation, and rendering-loss formulation remain mathematically equivalent. v2 displays and numbers previously stated equations more explicitly; it adds no theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: v2 replaces the foundation-model characterization throughout the title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion with a feedforward-model framing centered on AGP. This narrows the advertised model status while retaining the core claims about direct CT-to-Gaussian prediction, rapid preparation, generalization, composability, and optional fine-tuning.

C2.justification: v2 interprets AGP as necessary for convergence and attributes higher AGP point counts to reduced pruning, whereas v1 cited more initialized points. It removes the explicit lack-of-relighting limitation. It also makes ID superiority across all quality metrics explicit, despite unchanged LPIPS values of 0.097 for Render-FM and 0.096 for 6DGS, where lower is better.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies loss weights of 0.8/0.2, four sampled views and loss averaging, padding to multiples of 32, and half-resolution index scaling followed by the volume affine transformation. Conversely, redrawn Figure 2 omits channel widths and dropout rates shown in v1. Hardware, optimizer, label mappings, transfer-function values, and project-page access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the CTPelvic1K reference and cinematic-rendering references by Siemens and Wollschlaeger et al., while removing Ma et al.'s Segment anything in medical images. It revises the DVR discussion to acknowledge real-time local-illumination rendering and explicitly positions novelty in combining feedforward prediction, 6DGS, and AGP. Most cited research and relationships remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method and results passages are rewritten. Five contribution bullets become three, AGP receives a separate methodology subsection, and an ablation subsection precedes the baseline comparison. The conclusion's limitations and social-impact paragraphs are removed, and the title and author list change.

P2.justification: Both pipeline figures are redrawn, with Figure 1 adding rendering close-ups and PSNR annotations. v1 Figure 3's examples are enlarged and divided between v2 Figures 3 and 4. v2 adds Table A1, splits transfer-function Table S3 into Tables A4–A5, and substantially changes typography, text width, running headers, and table presentation.

improvement.justification: The independent CTPelvic1K test and newly documented training and coordinate details modestly strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The feedforward framing and clearer visual presentation improve precision and readability. These gains are tempered by the six-scan size of the added evaluation, removal of the relighting limitation and architecture details, and the unexplained change from 40 to 20 composability training views.
